req.title: Register requires username
req.statement: The system shall render the register form with an error message when POST /auth/register omits the username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /auth/register must render the register form with 'Username is required.' when username is omitted. We need: (1) a positive case confirming a valid registration succeeds (no error), (2) a negative case confirming omitting username yields the exact error message with HTTP 200, (3) a boundary case confirming an empty-string username (distinct from missing key) also triggers the error. Additional cases cover the exact error string constant, the status code, and both sides of the boolean guard to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_register_valid_username_succeeds
preconditions: App is initialised with a fresh temporary SQLite database
No prior registration for the test username exists
expected: No 'Username is required.' in response body
trace: R-FLASKR-004 — positive path: valid submission must NOT trigger the username error
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_valid_username_succeeds():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/register',
                    data={'username': 'newuser6', 'password': 'secret'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'
    assert b'Username is required.' not in r.data

test_register_valid_username_succeeds()
